in_ClaimDataJSON.description: Cleaned claim data from the Claims Eligibility step

in_PolicyDataJSON.description: Policy data as JSON from the Claims Eligibility step

in_EligibilityChecksJSON.description: Results of eligibility checks from Claims Eligibility Agent

in_CoverageChecksJSON.description: Coverage analysis results from Coverage Analysis Agent

in_PayoutChecksJSON.description: Payout calculation results from Payout Calculation Agent

in_SettlementJSON.description: The settlement table from the Payout Calculation Agent — see contracts/settlement-table.md. Carries recommended.net as a number, which is what the 20%-of-Coverage-A escalation rule compares against. Deliberately not required: if it fails to arrive the rule cannot be evaluated, and the prompt then requires escalation rather than a silent pass.

in_CredibilityChecksJSON.description: Credibility assessment results from Credibility Assessment Agent

in_EligibilityDecision.description: The human reviewer's decision at the eligibility gateway. An approval makes every finding in in_EligibilityChecksJSON a granted exception, not an open breach.

in_EligibilityNotes.description: The reviewer's own note explaining that decision. Where it contradicts a finding, the note wins.

out_FinalDecision.description: Final claims decision: approve, partial_approve, deny, or escalate

out_ReviewRequired.description: Whether a human must see this claim before any money moves. false sends it straight to settlement with nobody reading the amounts, so it is required rather than optional: a missing value would read as false and auto-settle an unchecked claim, whereas a required output that never arrives faults the job loudly. The case plan routes on this alone.

out_DecisionJSON.description: Full decision output including escalation flags, deny reasons, payout reference, and confidence level Check envelope — see contracts/check-envelope.md. Every string is shown to a human reviewer.

verdict.description: pass when nothing needs a human; attention when a reviewer should look; fail when this analysis blocks the claim.

headline.description: One line the reviewer can act on. States the reason, not the outcome.

summary.description: Your reasoning. Replaces the separate summary output that used to exist.

checks.description: One entry per thing you checked, reported whether it passed or not.

label.description: Sentence case, written for a claims reviewer. Never a payload field name.

status.description: warn when satisfied only with a caveat, or when data needed for the check was unavailable.

verdict.description: The one-line result shown beside the label.

details.description: Supporting evidence for this check, up to 6 rows. Supply it for every check, passing ones included — a reviewer can expand a passing check to see what was compared.
